strip: 105 cases, 12 at a time, ~46 min each
goal: Two or three new Venturis, changed in bore shape only, that hold a steady dose on piped flow from 6 to 100+ L/min, still dose at 6 L/min, and don't overflow the handpump. The top two get printed and bench tested the week of Nov 30.

requirements.note: Spread = highest ÷ lowest dose on piped flow (3-D CFD). 6–100 L/min is extrapolated from data to 60 L/min. The current part is on its own 3/4" train; V1 on the 1" long-radius reducer.

findings: Small throats overdose at high flow, large throats underdose at low flow. Best balance for 6–100 L/min is about a 16.5–17 mm throat.
Low-flow suction comes from the water column below the port; a slightly narrower outlet keeps that column intact.
Handpump weak dosing is air, not suction.
When the pump-head level drops below the inlet bore, air reaches the Venturi and the dose halves (two-phase CFD).
The current part overflows at 18.5 L/min.
V1 doesn't overflow below 30 L/min and stays within 0.1–1.5 mg/L on the bench; the new design must keep that.
actions_lab: 3-D check of finalists, both reducers, 6–120 L/min
CAD (threaded, water path probed), report, bench sheet
actions_bench: Needle-valve test: bleach flow at 5 / 10 / 20 / 40 cm suction
Pipe rig: dose + port suction at 6–100 L/min
Print and test the top two designs
